mine_p07_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_001.text: Day 505 began with a quarrel over a stool. Mu Ran had put it beside the practice bench to keep her sore knee away from the cold paving, and Guan Si moved it because its projecting leg obstructed the exit. Neither person was lying about what the stool did. Lin offered to shift the bench instead. That would have put the discharge line across the doorway. They finally carried a narrower seat from the store. By then the first appointment was ten minutes late, and the cost of a usable room had become wonderfully ordinary.

mine_p07_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_002.text: Wei Yan arrived carrying her own examination book and a cloth bag of calibrated comparison pieces. She was shorter than Lin had imagined from the firmness of her letters. A grey strand escaped her braid whenever she bent over a measurement. Before opening the book she asked who paid for the room, who would receive results, and whether anyone expected her to approve a candidate for the company. Guan answered the first question. Lin answered the second for herself. The third remained unanswered until Wei looked directly at the mine clerk waiting beside the doorway.

mine_p07_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_003.text: The clerk said the company wanted a capable small circuit practitioner available near the galleries. Wei asked whether that wish was written into Lin's instruction contract. It was not. She sent him to the public waiting bench rather than letting him stand behind the candidate. Lin felt embarrassed on his behalf and then relieved on her own. Desire for a local practitioner had made her seem valuable before she had demonstrated anything new. Wei would measure the person who actually sat at the bench, without measuring the employer's impatience alongside her.

mine_p07_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_004.text: Guan unfolded the terms agreed at the courtyard door. Twenty four coppers covered eight for instruction and rehearsal, six for three qualifying trial appointments, six for an independent examiner, and four for compatible consumable portions. The money came from Lin's already paid surface wages after her ordinary board, rather than an advance charged to a future certificate. She laid the counted coins down herself. One fell beneath the bench. Mu retrieved it with a walking stick and joked that the courtyard had already collected its first examination of patience. Nobody mistook the joke for a fee.

mine_p07_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_005.text: Lin had sixteen half day wages from the first eight weeks of common work, amounting to sixty four coppers. Thirty two had gone to eight weekly lodging and meal payments. The twenty four copper curriculum left eight from that particular block. Earlier receiving and short turn money stayed in her ordinary purse, with its own expenses, rather than being counted twice as training funds. The calculation disappointed her because it looked smaller than months of effort felt. It also meant the lessons belonged to her. A supervisor could not claim her body by paying the bill.

mine_p07_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_006.text: Wei read the rescheduling clause aloud because candidates rarely listened to it when healthy. An interrupted lesson or an unfit qualifying date could be moved while its unused appointment remained in the agreed course. A used appointment would remain used. The fee bought instruction, scheduled access, and examination work, not a result or unlimited treatment. If a clinician later required ordinary care, that would have to be arranged and paid separately. Lin wrote the distinction once in the margin. She wanted the rest of the morning to concern movement rather than the language of purchases.

mine_p07_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_007.text: The method book had a fresh page for the local small circuit examination. Wei dated it before any attempt and marked the standard as this school's practical criterion. Sixty units had to be actually usable after normal activity, sleep, and the sampling discharge. Compatibility had to reach ninety one percent. Controlled closure through the newly taught governing and conception routes also had to survive an interrupted ordinary breath, with a clean stop and grounded release. A large nominal reserve could satisfy none of that by merely existing. Wei crossed out the clerk's earlier phrase, promising capacity.

mine_p07_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_008.text: The earlier six pair qualification used a local minimum of forty eight usable units and ninety percent compatibility. Those numbers had extended the school's method beyond the older four pair record; Wei did not pretend an ancient text had supplied them. Lin's last actual comparison lay above both, but previous evidence did not guarantee this morning's condition. The courtyard would check her current prerequisite before offering new instruction. Mu, waiting for her own maintenance appointment, asked whether seven would make every familiar application stronger. Wei said their present input and duration limits stayed exactly where they were.

mine_p07_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_009.text: They began with the six primary pairs Lin already knew. Two upper limb pairs and the anterior and posterior lower limb pairs belonged to the older instruction. The later third upper limb pair and lateral lower limb pair had been learned from fixed primary trunk references, not discovered by guessing toward an unfamiliar destination. Lin could identify each taught route on her own body without treating a chalk picture as a substitute for sensation. The governing and conception bridges remained a new curriculum question. No one named an additional dantian or extraordinary vessel to make the diagram look impressive.

mine_p07_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_010.text: When Lin tried to explain the lateral pair, she spoke too quickly and shifted her waist to demonstrate the turn. Wei put the brush down. An anatomical reference was not an invitation to force a route with a theatrical twist. Lin straightened, breathed normally, and described where attention started and where it ended without moving her body to persuade the examiner. The second explanation was less memorable to an audience and more useful to someone repeating it. Mu asked a precise question about the return. Lin answered only the portion she had actually learned.

mine_p07_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_011.text: A small external comparison comb rested beside the bench. Its response could describe the surrounding field and help check that the consumable portion matched the agreed condition. It could not show Wei the inside of Lin's meridians. For that, the method combined Lin's reported sensation, bounded applications, controlled releases, and ordinary observations of her body over time. Guan checked the comb against a stored reference while Wei watched the candidate. Lin liked the division of attention. Nobody could make one glittering device do every kind of knowing they wanted from the room.

mine_p07_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_012.text: The sample discharge was taken before the usable quantity was written. Lin had to stop, settle, and wait for the comparison to finish; no one called the released amount available again because it had looked orderly leaving her. Fifty four and a half units remained actually usable, with ninety and a half percent compatibility. Wei wrote both values without multiplying one by the other a second time. Compatibility described the fit of the available quantity already measured as usable. Inflating or shrinking it through careless arithmetic would change the candidate on paper while leaving her body untouched.

mine_p07_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_013.text: Lin felt an old wish to apologize for the half percentage between her condition and the proposed new minimum. Wei had not asked her to possess the seventh stage yet. This appointment checked whether the existing six pair method could support careful preparation. She told Lin to distinguish a present deficit from a personal failure. Mu grinned at that and said she could supply enough personal failures for the whole morning if they needed some. Lin laughed, then noticed how much easier her shoulders felt once she stopped trying to defend a result no one had criticized.

mine_p07_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_014.text: For Day 506's maintenance task Wei required only the established ceiling: half a unit across four ordinary breaths, no more than an eighth in any breath, yielding a quarter of useful work. Guan set the bounded shoulder and waist task against a grounded dry fixture. The fixture stayed below shoulder height. Nobody would test an overhead catch or demand a sudden rescue movement. Lin checked the exit with her eyes before touching the prepared input. The empty path beside the narrow stool looked less trivial now that stopping had become part of the measurement.

mine_p07_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_015.text: She completed the first pair's task and released fully, then sat through the agreed rest instead of hurriedly presenting the next pair. The quarter unit of useful work did not return to her reserve because the fixture remained intact. The full half unit input had been consumed. Wei made her say that distinction in plain language. Lin had known it, yet hearing the subtraction aloud altered the appeal of a beautifully neat circuit. Efficiency mattered because there was a remainder she could spend, lose, or need later. The room would not supply it through praise.

mine_p07_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_016.text: Each of the other five primary pair tasks used its own bounded half unit and its own complete release. Between tasks Wei asked unrelated ordinary questions: whether Lin had eaten, which work shift she had accepted, whether the lodging roof still leaked. The questions were not riddles to reward a clever practitioner. A route needed to remain controllable while attention returned to life. By the sixth task Lin was tired of explaining Han's roof, but she did not shorten the rest. Six inputs had used three units. The measured remainder was fifty one and a half.

mine_p07_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_017.text: That remainder sat above the local six pair minimum, but Wei said the arithmetic alone had not earned a maintained qualification. They still watched how Lin walked across the paving, handled a cup, and described any tingling or delayed ache. Mu noticed a grain of grit beneath one foot and made her move before repeating the balance observation. Lin wanted to keep her good performance untouched. Instead she repeated an ordinary movement on a sound surface. A record that hid a bad floor to protect a good number would be a brittle record to build on.

mine_p07_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_018.text: The morning ended without a new stage. Wei gave Lin a short preparation reading and a prohibition on rehearsing the unfamiliar bridges alone. Guan reserved two further recovered maintenance mornings, Days 510 and 514, within the eight copper instruction portion. Lin would work her accepted ordinary shifts, sleep, and return without trying to preserve the sampled condition inside an artificial quiet week. She folded the page and discovered that she was excited despite having advanced nowhere. The route had become a real study problem instead of a distant word beside a realm name.

mine_p07_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_019.text: At midday Qiao Min stopped Lin beside the surface ledger and asked how soon the company could expect the small circuit. Lin said no date had been promised. Qiao rubbed an ink stain on her thumb and explained that a comparison post was being discussed for the next season. She had only asked so she could avoid promising another worker's availability. That was a reasonable question, and Lin's defensive answer had made it sound otherwise. They corrected the misunderstanding before it hardened. Qiao wrote available for ordinary assistant shifts beside Lin's name and left the future post blank.

mine_p07_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_020.text: The accepted work did not become lighter because Lin now had a curriculum. On the next half day she carried numbered labels between the covered inspection table and the outer receiving rack, leaving the heavy carrying to the workers assigned for it. A gust scattered three labels across red dust. She recovered two and replaced the dirty third from a clean copy rather than guessing at the faded number. The delay irritated Sui Jun, who had waited to close a crate entry. He gave her time to finish because a wrong plate number would outlast a quarter hour's annoyance.

mine_p07_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_021.text: Han's room was full that evening. A road crew had taken the spare sleeping platforms, and someone boiled noodles in a pot whose handle had been repaired too recently to inspire confidence. Lin moved her lesson book away from the steam. Lei An asked whether studying a new circuit made ordinary work feel foolish. Lin looked at the wet labels drying beside her sleeve and said it made ordinary work feel frighteningly good at finding mistakes. Lei laughed because that sounded like a complaint he had made about lamp maintenance. They ate before discussing either kind of route again.

mine_p07_022.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_022.text: One road worker told them a cousin had reached a higher stage merely by sitting beneath a rare root for a night. Mu, who had come for supper, asked who had examined the cousin afterward. The worker said the cousin had gone away. He might have been telling a true story about a stranger's impression; he could not supply the evidence they needed for their own bodies. Lin did not argue him out of his family pride. She asked what the cousin could now do without pain. The answer grew less certain and more interesting.

mine_p07_023.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_023.text: Guan visited the lodging with a stack of notices for a separate worker reading workshop. Three people wanted to understand the mine's eventual failed trial reports without purchasing a cultivation course. Mu Ran, Ou Sheng, and Ma Lian each chose a four copper place in the proposed followup session. The twelve coppers stayed in the courtyard's separate workshop envelope, held for that unused service. It did not pay Lin's lessons, wages, or future care. The participants expected useful public explanation, not private examination access. Guan told them a cancelled session would return their actual fees.

mine_p07_024.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_024.text: Ma Lian asked whether a reading workshop would make a timber leader responsible for recognizing a human route injury. Guan said it would help her read a reported limit and stop treating every practitioner as a universal tool. It would not qualify her to diagnose a body. That answer suited Ma better than a grander promise. Ou wanted to know which failed conditions would matter to ventilation scheduling. Mu wanted the next learner to see the hesitation normally removed from polished success stories. They bought the same proposed session for three very different reasons.

mine_p07_025.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_025.text: Lin disliked seeing coins placed beside a workshop that depended partly on what might happen to her. Mu said the session did not require her to fail. Even successful reports contained stopped attempts and excluded conditions, and the three workers could read those without demanding a spectacle. Lin agreed to let the future discussion use whatever redacted findings she actually authorized then, rather than granting permission for every private sensation in advance. Mu slid the envelope toward Guan, away from Lin. The arrangement no longer looked like an audience purchasing a seat inside someone else's body.

mine_p07_026.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_026.text: On Day 508 the mine bells rang for a delayed timber delivery. Lin had planned a reading hour, but her accepted assistant shift required counting replacement wedges beneath the covered inspection shelf. The wedges arrived damp at one end. Fan Luwei separated the suspect bundle and asked for its storage conditions before putting it anywhere near a support plan. Sui Jun wanted the whole consignment counted as received. Lin counted physical pieces and recorded the unresolved condition beside them. A completed quantity did not imply acceptance for structural use. That difference held up two other entries.

mine_p07_027.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_027.text: Fan eventually accepted the sound bundles and left the damp one for ordinary assessment. Sui complained that a small wet corner had become a whole morning's embarrassment. Lin could see why he hated a note that followed his goods after most of them were usable. She could also see Ma Lian inspecting the place where a bad wedge would have gone. Neither view let her erase the unresolved condition. When Sui asked who would pay for the delay, she referred him to the actual supply contract rather than inventing a sympathetic answer. His annoyance remained earned and survivable.

mine_p07_028.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_028.text: The argument stayed with Lin through supper and spoiled her concentration over the new reading. She kept returning to the supplier's face instead of the diagram. At first she treated that as proof of weak discipline. Then she noticed she had not eaten the bowl beside her. Reading difficult material while hungry and angry was not a cleaner form of commitment. She closed the book, ate, and told Mu what had happened. Mu disagreed with her handling of the last remark. They argued gently enough that both could still hear the missing part of the story.

mine_p07_029.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_029.text: On Day 510 Wei changed the waiting order. Lin ate before her appointment instead of afterward, worked an ordinary short morning errand, and sat through the courtyard's noise while another learner completed a maintenance check. The changed sequence was not a demand to conceal discomfort. Wei asked her to report it before sampling. Lin said her shoulder felt normal but her sleep had been broken by the road crew leaving before dawn. Wei could postpone if that affected control. They first observed ordinary movements and rested long enough to determine whether a valid maintenance comparison remained possible.

mine_p07_030.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_030.text: The sampling discharge again preceded the recorded available quantity. Lin's actual usable amount was fifty four and three quarters, compatibility ninety and a half percent. No one called the quarter unit difference growth toward the next stage. It could reflect recovered condition and ordinary measurement variation. The six bounded primary pair tasks together used three units and left fifty one and three quarters, with stops between them. Wei asked Guan to drop a folded cloth beside the doorway during the fourth rest. Lin looked, answered a question about it, and resumed only when directed. She never caught it through qi.

mine_p07_031.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_031.text: When the fifth task ended, Lin reported a fleeting prickling near her wrist. Wei stopped the sequence, asked where it had occurred, and had her rest before an ordinary touch comparison. The sensation cleared without loss of feeling or pain, but it still belonged in the record. After a sufficient quiet interval and a normal movement check, the final bounded task proceeded under supervision. Lin would rather have finished a perfectly smooth account. Wei preferred an accurate one. A harmless transient sensation could be assessed; an omitted sensation could only become a story someone regretted later.

mine_p07_032.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_032.text: Mu watched the final release with her elbows on the narrow stool and a face Lin could not read. Afterward she admitted that she envied Lin's clean report. Lin showed her the recorded interruption and the sleep note. That did not make their bodies identical or erase Mu's knee trouble. It gave the envy something more ordinary to compare. Mu said she had imagined Lin walking directly toward a certificate while everyone else spent money waiting. Lin said she was spending money waiting too. They stopped competing for the title of most delayed person and went to find lunch.

mine_p07_033.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_033.text: At the market awning a boy sold buns filled mostly with cabbage stems. Mu bought two and complained loudly enough that the boy's mother emerged to explain the flour price. The complaint became a negotiation for an extra spoonful of hot broth rather than a judgment on the family. Lin ate standing beside a dry wall and felt the cold begin to leave her fingers. A prospective circuit had not improved the weather or the contents of cheap buns. It had made her newly attentive to the ordinary meals without which her measured condition would mean much less.

mine_p07_034.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_034.text: That afternoon Lei showed Lin a damaged lamp housing. He had replaced the wick correctly, but a bent fastening let the glass rattle when the carrier turned. He wanted a second pair of eyes before telling the storekeeper he needed another housing. Lin held it still while he compared the fastening with a sound lamp. This was ordinary borrowed attention, not a cultivation application. They found the bend and marked the unit out of active use. Lei seemed relieved that the problem had a definite place. Lin envied that for a moment and then smiled at her own impatience.

mine_p07_035.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_035.text: The next night's lesson concerned what could be taught before the governing and conception bridges were opened in a supervised session. Wei's notes described posture, orientation, ordinary breathing, stopping cues, and the landmarks used for later attention. Lin could read those and rehearse the empty gestures without sending qi along an unfamiliar path. She practiced putting the cup down and standing from the bench slowly enough to keep her shoulders unstrained. Han accused her of studying how to grow old. She answered that several people at the mine seemed to have done it successfully and deserved careful observation.

mine_p07_036.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_036.text: Zeng Bo visited the room to borrow a cooking pot from Han. He had his own hammer back and a new private repair job, though the older lost work had not somehow returned. Lin noticed he no longer checked every peg beside the door before sitting. Their earlier tool disagreement had ended with facts, not an unlimited promise that the mine would never lose another object. Zeng asked about her studies with the cautious politeness of someone unsure whether cultivation questions were intimate. She described the stool argument. That gave him a problem he understood and a reason to laugh.

mine_p07_037.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_037.text: He offered to make a narrower study seat after his paid job was finished. Lin asked its price before accepting because he was still replacing the week's missing income. Zeng named a modest ordinary charge that she could consider later. She did not buy it that night. The existing stool was borrowed under the courtyard's room arrangements and worked safely enough. Declining a useful offer felt rude until Zeng said she had at least treated his work as something with a price. Their friendship could survive an unmade piece of furniture better than a favor neither person could afford.

mine_p07_038.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_038.text: On Day 512, Lin reread the next eight week agreement accepted on Day 505. Lin's work remained two four hour half days weekly at four coppers each, giving eight weekly when performed. Han's lodging and agreed meals cost four each week. The block had begun on Day 506, after the first closed. It would provide sixty four more wages through Day 561 and cost thirty two for those eight weeks of board. Qiao asked her to tell the scheduling clerk about lesson dates before gaps became absences. Lin wrote the appointments beside the shifts rather than promising to be everywhere.

mine_p07_039.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_039.text: A returning miner read the roster and asked why a learner with six pairs still carried labels instead of catching heavy loads. Qiao answered before Lin could. The assistant job was needed as written; a person's stage did not turn an unplanned overhead catch into a permitted application. The miner shrugged as though he had only been joking. Lin could not know how serious his expectation had been. She thanked Qiao afterward, then disliked needing the defense. Qiao said every roster contained people other workers imagined doing more than the paid task. Correcting that belonged to scheduling too.

mine_p07_040.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_040.text: The thought followed Lin to the practice court. She asked Wei whether learning a closed small circuit would eventually justify a sudden overhead catch. Wei refused to predict a task they had not assessed. This curriculum kept the existing half unit, four breath, shoulder and waist limits. A route could become more coordinated while those application limits stayed in force. Lin wrote that sentence where she could find it later. The mine's need for a dramatic rescue did not define her method. Its ordinary need for someone to stop a mistaken label before a crate moved remained real.

mine_p07_041.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_041.text: The third maintenance morning, Day 514, was colder and unusually quiet. Guan had shut one screen against dust but left the physical exit open. Wei asked Lin to examine the altered room before starting. The discharge fixture remained grounded and dry; the screen did not cross the release space. Lin pointed out a wet shoeprint near the waiting stool, and Guan wiped it away. These checks consumed no reserve. They used time and attention. Mu said the courtyard could improve its profits by charging for every wet shoeprint. Guan told her the floor would then become their most enthusiastic instructor.

mine_p07_042.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_042.text: Lin had slept through the night after completing an ordinary shift the previous afternoon. She reported the meal, the work, and the lack of unusual sensations before sampling. The actual usable quantity after discharge was fifty four and a half, compatibility ninety and three quarters percent. Wei used the unchanged bounded input for each of the six primary tasks. Lin stopped when a cart wheel struck the outer gate, waited for Guan to confirm the interruption had not changed the setup, and then continued on instruction. The noise did not become evidence of unusual control simply because it was loud.

mine_p07_043.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_043.text: The last release left fifty one and a half units after three total inputs, with the observed tasks still within shoulder and waist limits. Wei walked Lin through ordinary touch, grip, leg movement, and a short unhurried walk. Lin had no reported new pain or lost sensation. A candidate's clean answer did not replace looking at the actual movement. Wei compared what she could observe with Lin's account, and wrote any uncertainty instead of forcing the two into a perfect match. The assessment was a current maintenance comparison, not the independent new stage examination she had preregistered.

mine_exam_prior_practice.speaker: narrator
mine_exam_prior_practice.text: Lin read the three dated records together: Days 506, 510, and 514, with recovery, ordinary activity, sleep, sampling costs, bounded six pair tasks, interruptions, and the transient wrist report retained. Each began with actual usable quantity after sampling and subtracted the three units consumed by six tasks. Each ended with full release and an ordinary body check. These were prior practice evidence for careful supervised small circuit preparation. They did not demonstrate a governing or conception closure, meet the new sixty unit criterion, or confer stage seven. Wei signed that distinction before the instruction page turned.

mine_p07_045.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_045.text: The signature made Lin strangely sad. She had wanted a boundary clear enough to trust, then found that it also fenced off the tempting future she had imagined. Wei noticed her silence and asked whether she wished to continue. Lin said yes, but not because the records had nearly qualified her. They had shown that careful work could be repeated without hiding its interruptions. Wei accepted that answer. Mu tapped the table and said the records had also shown that everyone in the room needed to eat afterward. The sadness loosened when they began choosing where to go.

mine_p07_046.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_046.text: They walked to the surface market together, avoiding the fenced moth buffer where carts already had a marked detour. Jia Wen was kneeling beyond the fence with a cloth shade over a specimen tray, attending to ordinary observations rather than Lin's examination. Lin did not interrupt her for a symbolic blessing. She watched a cart take the longer line and remembered that the little habitat choice had made a real scheduling cost. Whatever role she had accepted there would return through actual work and evidence. It would not announce her body's future through an insect's wing.

mine_p07_047.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_047.text: A miner at the bread awning congratulated Lin on passing. She corrected him before the rumor reached the afternoon shift: she had completed maintenance comparisons and registered for supervised preparation. He looked disappointed, as if she had taken away a pleasant thing he was offering. Lin softened her voice without changing the facts. He wished her well anyway. Later she heard him telling another worker the less exciting version accurately. The effort mattered. A false certificate could travel through a workplace faster than the person it named, asking her to live up to something she had never claimed.

mine_p07_048.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_048.text: Mu bought flour from a woman who kept the scale visibly and asked whether Lin wanted to share supper. Lin's own room meal was already covered, so she offered company and help washing the borrowed pot instead of spending another meal's money without thinking. Mu preferred that to an unnecessary purchase. They sat beside Han's door while the flour seller packed the stall. Their conversation wandered through knees, lamps, poor handwriting, and every local school seemed to own a different kind of uncomfortable bench. None of it advanced a realm, and all of it filled the day.

mine_p07_049.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_049.text: That evening Lin copied only the new stopping cues into her work notebook. The detailed examination pages stayed protected at the lodging, not on a table where a supplier might read them while waiting. She wanted the cues available when she felt impatient, without turning her sensory report into a public object. Lei asked what the brief list meant. She explained the ordinary actions: stop, release, rest, report a change, do not force an unfamiliar route. He said lampkeepers had a version of the same list, except the fourth action usually involved admitting a cracked housing before someone carried it.

mine_p07_050.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_050.text: Mu told Lin why she kept the knee stool close. Her old walking injury had improved enough for work, then worsened when she accepted too many shifts because the household needed money. She did not want a higher stage to be another reason someone offered her more than she could carry. Lin had imagined Mu's delayed lessons as an interruption awaiting a triumphant end. Mu's account made a different shape. Reliable limits might let her continue a life already worth having, without a spectacular cure or a promotion.

mine_p07_051.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_051.text: Lin asked what work Mu hoped to keep. Mu repaired ordinary cloth screens used to separate dusty benches from waiting areas. Good screens needed measured gaps around the exit, sound fastenings, and fabric that could be washed without losing its fit. Her hands could do it while her knee rested. Lin promised no commission she lacked authority to give. She asked to watch the next repair if Mu wanted company. Mu said she wanted someone willing to hold a straight edge and stop talking when the measurements began.

mine_p07_052.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_052.text: Earlier that same afternoon Lin sat beside Mu's sewing table beneath the lodging eaves. The damaged screen smelled of dust and old soap. Lin held the edge while Mu measured the replacement patch, then lost her place when a miner called from the yard. Mu made her start again rather than smoothing over the error. The cloth was cheaper than a human body, but the habit mattered to both. They found a torn fastening hidden beneath a fold and sent that separate fault back to Guan with the repaired panel.

mine_p07_053.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_053.text: The miner who had called wanted directions to the receiving clerk, and Lin had given them without letting him enter the room. Mu said visitors often assumed a person sitting down was free to answer everything. Lin admitted she had assumed the same about Mu's waiting time. Neither apology needed a speech. They resumed the seam, and Lin kept one fingertip on the measured mark whenever she answered an ordinary question. Attention could be shared if the task allowed it. Where it could not, another person had to wait.

mine_p07_054.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_054.text: Guan inspected the repaired screen at the court before reinstalling it. The patch was sound; the old fastening required replacement by the person responsible for the frame. Mu's invoice covered cloth work, with that exclusion plainly noted. Lin saw how the little screen could have become a dispute if everyone called it simply fixed. Guan paid the agreed repair charge from the room maintenance fund, not candidate fees reserved for another purpose. Mu pocketed her own wages. The screen returned to use after its fastening was separately made sound.

mine_p07_055.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_055.text: Lin compared this with the proposed circuit in her reading. It was tempting to think of a body as a room with six familiar openings and two newly purchased fastenings. Wei warned against taking the resemblance literally. Landmarks and instructional diagrams were tools for learning, not proof that living tissue behaved like timber or cloth. Lin had to report sensation and observe control in the taught method. A good analogy could help her remember to check an exit. It could also conceal the precise point where knowledge stopped.

mine_p07_056.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_056.text: Wei showed her an old teaching copy with a beautifully continuous line drawn through an uncertain passage. A previous pupil had darkened the line to make the diagram easier to remember. The ink had survived while the pupil's qualifications and circumstances had not. Wei kept the page because it showed why attractive drawings required a source. Lin traced the darkened portion with the end of a brush, without copying it into her own route. She asked which landmarks were actually taught here. Wei turned to the corrected instruction sheet.

mine_p07_057.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_057.text: The answer took most of an ordinary hour. By the end Lin had a shorter list of references and a longer list of questions for supervised preparation. She disliked how little of the beautiful diagram remained available. Then Wei asked her to explain the corrected sheet back. Lin could distinguish taught reference, later lesson, and unresolved comparison without pretending to have crossed any of them. That was a better beginning than a whole imagined circuit. Guan rang the appointment bell, and Wei put the old drawing safely away.

mine_p07_058.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_058.text: At the lodging Lin found Lei repairing a strap by lamplight. He let her hold the loose end while he fitted the buckle. She wanted to tell him everything about the disputed drawing, but he needed quiet to finish the small job. When the strap was secure he asked what had happened at the court. Lin gave him the uncertain line rather than a heroic account of new knowledge. Lei said old lamp plans could carry the same seductive mistake. Someone's neat repair became everyone's inherited fact unless a later worker looked closely.

mine_p07_059.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_059.text: Han listened while mending a sleeping mat and said the hardest instruction was usually admitting the change. A younger lodger had once continued a road job through fever because he was afraid of losing his bed. Han had seen the consequences and changed how he collected late weekly payments, though he could not afford to provide indefinite free rooms. Lin looked at the repaired mat and understood why a paid recovery plan would need money as well as kindness. At that moment she was healthy enough to treat the lesson as a warning. Later it would have a sharper edge.

mine_p07_060.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_060.text: The first week's fees and work entries were complete. Guan had used the agreed instruction appointments; the three qualifying trial site slots and independent examination remained for later dates. The separate twelve copper workshop envelope still held Mu, Ou, and Ma's four copper deposits for a service not yet delivered. Lin checked the distinction once because a shared courtyard ledger could make funds look more interchangeable than they were. Guan let her see the totals without opening other candidates' private pages. The money was finite, owned, and attached to particular work. That clarity let the room turn back toward teaching.

mine_p07_061.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_061.text: Before sleeping Lin traced the six primary reference landmarks with an ordinary fingertip, sending no qi into the unlearned bridge. Her hand stopped at the point where the next lesson would begin. She could imagine a circuit in a diagram, but imagination did not make a route usable. Outside, a cart rolled through the yard and a worker called to have the gate opened. Lin recognized the voice, heard the reply, and felt the room settle around the familiar noise. Preparation had given her a narrower question and people who could help answer it. Morning would require learning slowly.

mine_p07_062.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_062.text: In the morning Han burned the first pot of porridge while arguing with a carrier about borrowed bedding. Lin helped scrape the sound portion into bowls, then ate before leaving. The lost food was a small real cost, and Han would replace it from his own kitchen money. Neither lesson nor argument made warm ordinary breakfast optional.

mine_p07_063.speaker: narrator
mine_p07_063.text: At the practice court door the next lesson notice already carried Day 515. Wei had chosen a short preparation session followed by ordinary work rather than a secluded retreat. Lin would be asked to keep the learned parts sound while new landmarks were introduced one at a time. She put the notice beneath her room key so she could not leave without seeing both. The key meant a bed she paid for; the notice meant her chosen method. Neither was a token of destiny. Together they made the coming week possible enough to approach without inventing its result.
